The founder test is reasonably specific but does not name a specific Agorapulse page element or evidence anchor — 'feeling words vs result words' is slightly generic and could appear in another teardown.

requiredFixes: Rewrite the ## section heading to include at least one searchable term — for example: 'Agorapulse Homepage Messaging Evolution: From Simplicity to ROI'.

Split the third H3 block into two separate H3 sub-blocks: one for the section-heading evidence (warmth vs evidence), one for the buyer-persona implication — each must open with its takeaway in the first sentence.

Rewrite the paragraph beginning 'The H1 and the section headings point in the same direction' so the closing sentence is concrete or actionable, not a conditional hedge ('if the rest of the evidence holds').
Check the paragraph quoting the full meta description in H3 two — trim it to under 60 words or split the quote into a callout and keep the analytical sentence separate.

Anchor the founder test more tightly to Agorapulse's specific evidence — for example: 'On Agorapulse's current homepage, tally every word in the H1, subheadline, and first section heading that describes a feeling versus a reportable result — then run the same count on your own homepage'.
riskFlags: Phrase 'That removal may signal a de-emphasis of price-sensitivity as a primary draw' — appropriately hedged with 'may signal', acceptable.

Phrase 'consistent with a page-wide shift, not a single headline swap, if the rest of the evidence holds' — the conditional hedge salvages the causal risk but makes the sentence read as abstract rather than actionable.

Phrase 'may now resonate most with marketing professionals who report upward' — buyer-persona inference not directly traceable to evidence; hedged with 'may' which is acceptable, but the specific characterisation 'report upward' is an inference beyond the evidence note which says 'marketing professionals and team leads who must justify spend'.
seoNotes: The ## section heading contains no searchable terms — this will hurt organic discovery for queries like 'Agorapulse messaging strategy' or 'Agorapulse homepage evolution'.
The H3 headings do contain 'Agorapulse' plus topic terms ('headline shift', 'page title', 'meta description', 'messaging shift') which are good secondary keyword anchors.
The section correctly names the primary keyword evidence elements (H1, meta description, page title) that match the article's SEO intent around 'Agorapulse homepage teardown'.
Quoting the exact before/after headlines and page titles verbatim is strong for long-tail query matching — keep this pattern.
rewriteInstruction: Fix the ## heading first — replace the clever narrative title with one that includes 'Agorapulse', 'messaging', and a topic term such as 'homepage' or 'positioning'. Then split the third H3 block into two: the first covering the section-heading evidence (warmth-to-evidence shift with the specific quoted headings), the second covering the buyer implication (who the new language is written for). Each new H3 block must open with its takeaway in sentence one. Trim the meta description paragraph to under 60 words by separating the verbatim quote from the analysis. Rewrite the conditional closing sentence ('if the rest of the evidence holds') into a concrete observation — for example, note that the H1, section headings, and page title all drop ease-of-use language simultaneously, which makes this a structural shift rather than a single copy tweak. Finally, tighten the founder test by naming Agorapulse's specific elements as the reference point before asking the founder to apply the same count to their own page.
